facts: On 23 October 1995, P.W.10 one Shantabai and her son Satish had gone to the market for purchasing Puja articles and some fire crackers.
When they returned home they found that Nisha (the daughter of Satish aged 3 years) was not at home.
The efforts of all the members of the family to find out the young girl bore no fruits. Therefore, a missing report was lodged with the police station.
On 24 October 1995 P.W.6 one Tanhabai Davkar went to the field to cut grass.
There she noticed the dead body of a young girl lying among the sugarcane crop.
Tanhabai then informed her son P.W.12 one Sitaram Deokar that she had seen a body lying in the sugarcane field.
In the meantime, Shantabai came to the police station to make enquiries.
She was informed that there was the dead body of a young girl lying in the field.
Shantabai identified the dead body to be that of her granddaughter Nisha.
issues: The legal questions or points of law being debated
petitioner_arguments: The evidence of two child witnesses, Ashif Fakir and Ramzan, who saw the Respondent carrying a jute bag with blood dripping from it.
respondent_arguments: The High Court disbelieved the evidence of these two child witnesses on various grounds.
court_reasoning: The trial Court put several questions to ascertain whether the two child witnesses were aware of the sanctity of oath and whether they were able to understand the questions put to them.
The trial Court found that the two child witnesses had answered all the questions properly.

The evidence of a child witness must be evaluated more carefully and with greater circumspection because a child is susceptible to be swayed by what others tell him and thus a child witness is an easy prey to tutoring.
holding: The Supreme Court set aside the order of conviction and acquitted the Respondent of all offences.
